newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mint tender set to push zinc premiums lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mint tender set to push zinc premiums lower.

text.p: Physical market zinc premiums in the United States look set to tumble following the U.S. Mint tender on Tuesday, dealers said.
Traders said the winners looked to be Trademet, MG, Hochschild Partners and Bal at premiums ranging from 3.55 to 4.75 cents a lb over LME cash.
Previously, U.S. premiums were quoted at 4.25 to 4.75 cents a lb.
The official result of the 2,600 tonne special high grade (SHG) metal tender is due soon.
Dealers pointed out that with the LME nearby zinc market moving into a backwardation, or cash premium, over forward months, it is difficult to finance the storage of metal.
LME cash to three months zinc backwardation was $11/$13 Wednesday.
Months further forward have been in backwardation for some time.
But with much of the world's zinc stocks seen as being tightly held, some dealers doubt if much metal will be dumped on the market because of the backwardation's effect on storage costs.
Another dampener on premiums is the summer lull in the nothern hemisphere.
In addition, the price of zinc on LME soared to seven-year highs this week as technical tightness, as reflected in the backwardation, grips the market amid falling stocks, traders said.
Such price surges also dampen premiums.

"It's not unusual that at times when the LME price goes up, premiums tend to go down because some producers feel they are getting it in the price, so they can give a little back in the premium," a producer-linked dealer said.
Also in the U.S., the presence of much off-grade metal on the market is also taking support away from the premium, a dealer said.
